question: Is Uber's 31.6% slide to $63.47 a bargain on $10.42B FCF, or a Stage 4 trap masked by SBC, $17.1B M&A, >$10B AV commitments, and Waymo's Jan 2028 break?

epigraph.quote: Headline cash flow tells you what worked yesterday; balance-sheet footnotes and AV commitments tell you what changed today; the Stage 4 tape tells you to stay out of the way.
epigraph.author: Executive Underwriting Summary

web_blocks.html: What Uber Does & What Changed: Uber runs the largest global ride and delivery network across 70+ countries [1, 31]. Q3 2026 reached 215M monthly users, $59.82B in Gross Bookings (+20% YoY), and $10.42B in TTM Free Cash Flow [31, 32]. Yet our Pass 1 audit found five big shifts. First, Waymo plans to end Austin and Atlanta exclusivity with its own app in January 2028 (>500k weekly trips) [40]. Second, Uber committed >$10B to AV equity and fleet deals (>120k AVs, 35k+ Lucid/Nuro) [41]. Third, Delivery Hero's offer hit 66.56% (H2 2027 close) amid EC/KFTC/MENA scrutiny, lifting debt +49% to $15.66B and cutting Q3 buybacks 75% [31, 43]. Fourth, DoorDash bought Deliveroo for £2.9B in October 2025 [42]. Fifth, Q4 2026 faces a ~$1.5B UK VAT outflow, the Dec 2 EU Platform Work Directive, Australia's >AUD $100M tax ruling, and the FTC Uber One lawsuit [39, 44, 45].

Our Independent Dual Verdict: Core quality stays COMPOUNDER_PASS with kpi_health: PASS_WITH_WATCH. We deduct $2.15B SBC, $7.67B net debt/leases, $1.50B Q4 UK VAT cash, $10.65B net M&A outlays, and -$0.50B/yr for AV and regulatory drag. That puts shares at 18.16x normalized EV/FCF ($8.22B FCF_0). Our independent DCF sets Base value at $70.00 (+10.3%), Bear at $42.00 (-33.8%; $38.19 stressed), and Bull at $105.00 (+65.4%). Weighted 12-month expected value is just $67.20 (+5.9%). Shares closed Nov 20 at $63.47 ($64.60 live Nov 23) in Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED) during a 10-day US Downtrend (35.8% breadth >50DMA). New equity is strictly REJECTED (TIER_0; TREND, CASH_FLOW) and common shares are NOT_HELD (0 shares). On the 5 open Robinhood Dec 17, 2027 LEAPS (4x $110C, 1x $100C; 392 DTE Nov 20 / 389 DTE Nov 23), we mandate EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH) into USD cash.

Long-Term (2–5 Years): COMPOUNDER_PASS (PASS_WITH_WATCH). Track Delivery Hero de-leveraging (<2.0x), Lucid/Nuro AV unit ROIC, and Mobility take rates (>23%) before committing new capital [31, 40, 41, 43].

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our freshly audited, independent institutional dossier on Uber Technologies as of the November 20, 2026 verified market session. Rather than taking prior conclusions on faith, we ran a price-blind Pass 1 audit of Uber's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q, earnings call, competitive landscape, and regulatory docket—and uncovered five material structural shifts that fundamentally reshape the investment case.

Operationally, Uber's core marketplace remains impressive: 215 million monthly active users, 4,061 million quarterly trips, $59.82 billion in Q3 Gross Bookings (+20% YoY), and $10.42 billion in trailing twelve-month Free Cash Flow. Yet beneath that headline strength, five major headwinds have converged: (1) Waymo confirmed it is ending Uber exclusivity in Austin and Atlanta to launch its standalone Waymo One app in January 2028 after surpassing 500,000 weekly paid trips; (2) Uber pivoted away from pure asset-lightness by committing over $10 billion toward AV equity stakes and future fleet procurement covering more than 120,000 vehicles (anchored by 35,000-plus Lucid/Nuro robotaxis); (3) Delivery Hero's tender offer reached 66.56% acceptance (targeting H2 2027 close) amid European, Korean, and Middle Eastern antitrust scrutiny over Uber's loan backing the SSW Partners carve-out, lifting long-term debt 49% to $15.66 billion and cutting Q3 buybacks 75%; (4) DoorDash completed its £2.9 billion acquisition of Deliveroo in October 2025; and (5) CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy flagged a ~$1.5 billion Q4 2026 FCF hit from the UK HMRC VAT dispute, right alongside the December 2, 2026 EU Platform Work Directive transposition deadline, Australia's 6–1 payroll tax ruling exceeding AUD $100 million, and the FTC plus 21-state Uber One ROSCA lawsuit.

When we re-underwrite valuation independently in Pass 2—deducting $2.15 billion in annualized stock-based compensation, $7.67 billion in net debt and operating leases (keeping $11.37 billion of restricted insurance collateral separate), $1.50 billion in Q4 UK VAT cash, $10.65 billion in net pending M&A outlays, and $0.50 billion per year for recurring AV commercialization and regulatory drag—Uber's $63.47 close equates to 18.16 times normalized pro-forma EV-to-FCF, not the flattering 12.44 times headline ratio. Our independent DCF sets Base fair value at $70.00 (+10.3%), Bear at $42.00 (-33.8%; $38.19 combined stress with the $2.34 billion uncollateralized insurance gap), and Bull at $105.00 (+65.4%), producing a thin $67.20 12-month expected value (+5.9%).

Layered on top of a confirmed Stan Weinstein Stage 4 breakdown at $63.47 (with Monday November 23's modest bounce to $64.60 failing to repair a single moving average) inside a 10-distribution-day US market Downtrend (35.8% breadth above 50DMA), our New-Capital Verdict is strictly REJECTED (TIER_0; reasons: TREND and CASH_FLOW). We keep 100% of marginal cash in reserve—our $7,290.91 consolidated US cash ($4,772.99 Schwab plus $2,517.92 Robinhood) equals 9.13% of our $79,861.16 net worth, well below the 22.0% Downtrend cash floor—leaving Stage 2 candidates ABBV and ACGL at 0% until liquidity recovers.

Finally, while equity accounts hold zero common Uber shares (NOT_HELD), Robinhood holds 5 open December 17, 2027 Call LEAPS (4x $110C and 1x $100C; $3,463.86 cost; $1,775.86 recorded mark; 392 DTE Nov 20 / 389 DTE Nov 23). Because both strikes expire at $0.00 intrinsic value at our $70.00 Base Case—and all four $110 calls STILL expire worthless even at our $105.00 Bull Case—we override the mechanical scanner and mandate EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH) via limit orders on relief-bounce liquidity into USD cash, with zero averaging down and hard invalidation at or below $63.00. Chapters 1 through 9 below walk through every operating driver, footnote, valuation input, and decision rule in full.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: TRUST THE NUMBERS, NOT THE HEADLINE MULTIPLE
book_callouts.text: Uber's core business is strong, yet five newly uncovered shifts—Waymo's Jan 2028 break, >$10B in AV commitments, Delivery Hero leverage, DoorDash-Deliveroo, and UK/EU/FTC regulatory drains—compress expected value to +5.9% inside a Stage 4 downtrend. Discipline means rejecting new equity today and closing all 5 out-of-the-money Dec 2027 LEAPS into cash.
